record.paper_title: Some of my favorite open problems
record.context_brief: Can one hear the degree threshold
record.original_question: Suppose f and g are circle-valued maps on S^1 with identical Fourier-modulus data |a_n(f)|=|a_n(g)| for all integers n. Is the known positive conclusion deg f=deg g, which holds for f,g∈W^{1/3,3}(S^1;S^1) and for Hölder maps C^{0,α} with α>1/3, still valid for rougher classes such as W^{1/p,p}(S^1;S^1) with p>3 or C^{0,α}(S^1;S^1) with α≤1/3? The problem remains open even in mixed-regularity cases where one map is above and the other below the 1/3 threshold.

evidence.quote: Open Problem 5.5. What happens to Theorem 5.5 when f, g ∈ W1/p,p(S1;S1) with p > 3 (resp., f, g ∈ C0,α(S1;S1) with α ≤ 1/3)? The problem is open even under the stronger assumption that f ∈ W1/p,p with 2 < p ≤ 3 and g ∈ W1/q,q with q > 3 (resp., f ∈ C0,α with α > 1/3 and g ∈ C0,β with β ≤ 1/3).

artifact.category_tag: Sobolev maps to the circle and topological degree
artifact.status_search_result: The question is stated as an open problem in Brezis's collection of favorite open problems and in the Brezis–Mironescu monograph "Sobolev Maps to the Circle" (2021). No subsequent work found resolving it for $W^{1/p,p}$ with $p>3$ or Hölder exponent $\alpha\le 1/3$, including the mixed-regularity cases. The problem appears to remain open.
